messages:
Taylor: Hey team - need urgent help. My PCP referred me to an oncologist after a biopsy showed a suspicious mass. The clinic we want to use (Northside Oncology) is out-of-network for my Redwood medical plan. They say treatment would start within 31 days and need pre-authorization for chemo planning. What do I need to get an exception review for in-network benefits or an expedited OON prior auth? I'm attaching the biopsy pathology report and the referral letter when I upload.

Ruth (People Ops): Sorry you're dealing with this, Taylor. For OON exception reviews we typically need: 1) pathology report (scanned PDF), 2) referral/consult note from PCP, 3) oncology consult note or proposed treatment plan from the OON clinic with estimated CPTs/HCPCS and dates, 4) cost estimate or range from the provider, and 5) any supporting docs showing lack of appropriate in-network specialists locally if applicable.

Ruth (People Ops): Important: also sign the HIPAA release/authorization so our team can speak with the carrier and the OON provider on your behalf. Use secure upload (link below) or email benefits@redwood.com with subject "OON oncology exception - Taylor - [DOS window]". Mark as EXPEDITE if treatment window is <2 weeks.

Dr. Lee (Oncology): I can prepare the consult/treatment plan. For prior auth please include these codes we usually request: 96413, 96415 (chemo infusion), 74177 if CT staging done, 77014 for radiation consult if needed. I'll include estimated cycles and a short medical necessity paragraph. If carrier needs pathology slides review, we can request a rapid peer-to-peer review.

Taylor: Do you know how often carriers grant full in-network parity for OON oncology? If they deny, what's the fallback for scheduling quickly?

Ruth (People Ops): Carriers will grant exceptions when there's clinical justification or lack of timely in-network access. Success depends on: (a) medical necessity letter from treating oncologist; (b) documentation that in-network options cannot meet the required timeframe (dates of attempted appointments); (c) cost estimate and willingness to negotiate a case rate sometimes helps. If carrier denies, options: 1) appeal with peer-to-peer and expedited review, 2) request a case management review which can sometimes negotiate direct-billing rates with the provider, or 3) use an in-network provider but request a rapid consult to transfer care if clinically acceptable. We'll coordinate whichever path you prefer.

Taylor: If we ask for a peer-to-peer, do I need to be present on the call? Will Dr. Lee do it?

Dr. Lee (Oncology): I can do the peer-to-peer with the carrier MD. Usually patient presence isn't required but helpful if you want to be on the line. I'll prepare a focused summary and cite urgency.

Ruth (People Ops): Timeline: submit complete packet & authorization = carrier decision often within 3-10 business days for expedited oncology reviews; if they request peer-to-peer it's usually scheduled within 48-72 hours. Upload the docs here: https://benefits.redwood.com/secure-upload (choose "OON Exception/Oncology"). Use subject "EXPEDITE - Oncology OON Exception - Taylor".

ClaimsBot: Templates and links: HIPAA release: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/hipaa-release.pdf. Medical necessity template: https://benefits.redwood.com/templates/med-necessity-oncology.docx. Upload portal: https://benefits.redwood.com/secure-upload (select "Claims - OON Exception"). For status updates check: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims/status and reference claim request ID we assign after upload.

Taylor: Uploading pathology, referral, and Dr. Lee's initial plan now. I added the clinic cost estimate and requested the HIPAA release link be emailed. Please EXPEDITE 1 - treatment window starts in ~10 days. Appreciate you coordinating. :heart:
